original_verdict.psd_statement: The implication is valid. Since eps>0, normalization denominators are positive. Equal alpha vectors make the unnormalized response vectors proportional by a positive scalar. Thus tr(rho H) is proportional to tr(rho0 H)=0. For PSD rho and H, zero trace product forces support(rho) into ker(H); a one-dimensional kernel and trace one then give rho=rho0. This certifies uniqueness even among mixed states, but failure to construct this sufficient certificate proves neither certificate infeasibility nor a collision. Neither numerical construction is a certificate.
original_verdict.local_statement: The stated real and imaginary derivatives are correct for Hermitian C_i. The nonzero exact 14x14 minor gives an invertible derivative for 14 selected outputs on the 14-real-dimensional projective chart. The inverse function theorem therefore yields neighborhood-wise injectivity for pure rays and local determination of the mean Born response. The claim applies to the unit-normalized rational stored-state snapshot only: it establishes neither mixed-state uniqueness, global pure-state uniqueness, a quantified neighborhood, stable inversion nor an exact native-circuit result.
original_verdict.native_family_statement: The analytic counterexample is valid under the stated circuit order and parameterization. With zero preparation rotations, every word state is |000>; with only the specified query RY active, both CNOT rings preserve the |000> amplitude. Consequently mu=cos^2(theta/2), while constant per-token responses yield alpha_i=1/T despite different mu values. Finite atanh(theta/pi) realizes both proposed angles. With fixed utilities and downstream inputs, identical alpha gives identical pooled rowlogits. This is an exact native parameter-family counterexample at a degenerate word frame, not a collision in the original trained frame or evidence of useful discarded information.
